edges.note: 1990 McCarthy paper explicitly quotes and evaluates the 1959 Advice Taker prospectus.
Both use justification/dependency structure for contradiction-driven repair; do not infer direct lineage from chronology alone.
ATMS paper explicitly contrasts conventional justification-based TMSs with ATMS.
GDE explicitly uses assumption-based truth maintenance for candidate maintenance and measurement selection.
Hou explicitly formalizes measurement/discrimination issues arising in Reiter/de Kleer diagnosis lineages.
Hou explicitly builds from Reiter diagnosis and adds measurement theory.
Both compact sets of viable alternatives, but use different hypothesis/support structures.
Both maintain multiple live alternatives and prune/compress them under new evidence; no shared implementation implied.
Both select observations/queries to discriminate among live candidates using different formal criteria.
Both exploit dependency structure to avoid destructive chronological rollback.
GRASP paper explicitly notes TMS/CSP nogoods as similar conditions to conflict-induced clauses.
GRASP situates conflict-induced clauses relative to CSP nogood/conflict methods.
Kambhampati explicitly unifies intelligent backtracking and failure-driven explanation learning under refinement search.
Both value computation/reasoning by downstream utility; exact historical citation chain not asserted here.
Both make evidence acquisition part of the task, though AR-Bench evaluates broad active reasoning rather than QBC specifically.
Both center change under new evidence; Belief-R is an LLM evaluation framework rather than AGM implementation.
Support/currentness revision reappears as stale-memory invalidation problem.
Both motivate representation-sensitive reasoning, but one is explicit symbolic engineering and the other latent neural geometry.
Both maintain evolving multiple hypotheses; support-set vs particle/weight semantics differ materially.
